solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Morse with two idiots wanting leads

indicators.note: lacking their leads means each of the two words loses its opening letter

parts.note: first idiot: diddy is a Scots word for a fool
second idiot: numpty is a Scots word for a stupid person

explanation.surface: Inspector Morse finds himself saddled with two idiots who have no leads in a case.
explanation.walkthrough: DIDDY and NUMPTY each lose their first letter to make IDDY-UMPTY. Morse sounds like the TV detective but is the code.
explanation.definitionFit: Iddy-umpty is a jocular name for Morse code, imitating the sound of its dots and dashes.

clue.text: Creased skirt in reproduction, nothing excluded

indicators.note: something excluded is shut out, so nothing is taken away from the result
one word sits inside another, so the skirt goes within the reproduction

parts.note: a copy is a reproduction
to skirt is to run along the rim or edge; here the noun
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A cheap copy of a skirt came out creased, with nothing left out of the reproduction.
explanation.walkthrough: Skirt as a verb means to go round the edge, which gives the noun for that edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimpy describes something crimped, with small folds or wrinkles pressed into it.

clue.text: Indifferent couple of broadcasts heard

indicators.note: what is heard is judged by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: to broadcast seed is to sow it; two of them

explanation.surface: Someone hears a pair of radio broadcasts and is left indifferent.
explanation.walkthrough: Broadcast in its farming sense means scattering seed, so the word wanted is sow, said twice.
explanation.definitionFit: So-so means mediocre or middling, neither good nor bad.

clue.text: Fenced with royal support so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak asks for words as they are spoken, sound rather than spelling

parts.note: the Palace stands for royalty, and aided means supported

explanation.surface: An estate was fenced off with help from the royal household.
explanation.walkthrough: The Palace is shorthand for the royal household, so royal support is the Palace having aided.
explanation.definitionFit: A palisade is a fence of pointed stakes, so palisaded means enclosed by such a fence.

clue.text: General coming from local, left in charge

parts.note: the local is one's nearest pub
standard abbreviation
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: An army general emerges from the local bar, leaving someone else in command.
explanation.walkthrough: A local is British slang for the pub nearest your home.
explanation.definitionFit: Public as an adjective means general, belonging to or concerning everyone.

clue.text: Jam sandwiches soft for a little girl

indicators.note: a sandwich holds its filling between two outer layers, so one word encloses another

parts.note: to jam is to lock fast, as a stuck mechanism does
a soft is a softy, a fool

explanation.surface: A jam sandwich made with soft bread is just the thing for a small child.
explanation.walkthrough: Soft is used as a noun meaning a silly person, a softy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassock is a Scots diminutive of lass, a young girl.

clue.text: Southern Ireland introduces rolling maul that's feigned

indicators.note: something rolling tumbles over, so the letters of the word maul are mixed

parts.note: standard abbreviation

indicators.note: to introduce is to bring in, so the Irish abbreviation takes the mixed letters inside it

parts.note: IR is an abbreviation for Ireland
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A rugby report: a southern Irish side brings in a rolling maul that turns out to be a dummy.
explanation.walkthrough: A rolling maul is a rugby move where a group of players binds together and drives forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Simular is an old word meaning counterfeit or pretended, related to simulate.

clue.text: Relish removing top recently? Long ago

definitions.note: the whole phrase: 'recently' in a sense used long ago

indicators.note: taking off the top of a down answer drops its first letter

parts.note: a palate is a taste or relish for something

explanation.surface: Someone has recently lost their appetite, or was it long ago?
explanation.walkthrough: PALATE loses its P. The question mark and 'Long ago' flag that the meaning 'recently' is archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Alate is an archaic adverb meaning lately, of late.

clue.text: Record damned poet's revealed

parts.note: a gramophone record is a disc
a damned soul is lost

explanation.surface: A record has revealed a damned poet's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poet's' marks a form used by Spenser, not modern English.
explanation.definitionFit: Disclost is Spenser's past participle of disclose, meaning uncovered or made known.

clue.text: Former simply vile rule ignored

indicators.note: what is ignored is left out, so that letter drops away

parts.note: earthly can mean base or worldly, the opposite of heavenly
R is an abbreviation for rule

explanation.surface: In former times one simply ignored a vile law.
explanation.walkthrough: EARTHLY loses its R. 'Former' marks the answer as an obsolete word.
explanation.definitionFit: Eathly is an old form meaning easily, so simply in the sense of without difficulty.

clue.text: Driver has week in Glasgow, thoroughly wet there

parts.note: Dr is an abbreviation for driver
ouk is the Scots word for week

explanation.surface: A driver spends a week in Glasgow and gets soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There' points back to Glasgow: the answer is a Scots word too.
explanation.definitionFit: Drouk is Scots for drench, to make thoroughly wet.

clue.text: Leader retiring can secure backing re early transitional period

indicators.note: the leader steps down, so the opening letter goes

parts.note: the can is slang for a toilet, as is kazi

indicators.note: backing means running in the opposite direction, so the word is read right to left

parts.note: to nail something down is to secure it

explanation.surface: A party leader steps down, but the can is secured on his behalf.
explanation.walkthrough: Kazi and can are both British slang for a lavatory; 're' is just 'about', joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Azilian is the Mesolithic culture that bridged the Old and New Stone Ages in western Europe.

clue.text: Reveal lady's bust

parts.note: Di, short for Diana, is the crossword's usual lady; with the apostrophe S
bust and bosom both mean a woman's chest

explanation.surface: A woman reveals her bust.
explanation.definitionFit: To disbosom is to unburden oneself, to make known what one has kept hidden.

clue.text: Shock as before leaving New York is concerning

indicators.note: when something is leaving it departs, so the abbreviation that follows is taken away

parts.note: astony is an obsolete verb meaning to stun or astonish
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: It is a shock to hear that someone has left New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As before' marks an archaic word for shock, an old form of astonish.
explanation.definitionFit: As to is a prepositional phrase meaning about or with regard to.

clue.text: Sulphur left out, paint mostly blended as before

indicators.note: to paint is to work colours over a surface, so the letters are reworked
something left out is omitted, so that element is removed

parts.note: the word taken as written, as fodder
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: A painter leaves out the sulphur yellow, and the paint is mostly mixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left out' reads as S being removed from MOSTLY; 'paint' then mixes the remaining letters. 'As before' marks an archaic form.
explanation.definitionFit: Ymolt is an old past participle of melt, and melted things run together.

clue.text: Makeshift court house during stoppage accepted

indicators.note: something happening during a period sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a cut in supply is a stoppage
CH is an abbreviation for court house
A is the abbreviation for accepted, as on a bill

explanation.surface: A temporary court house was set up during a strike, and that was accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is a dictionary abbreviation for court house; A for accepted is used on bills of exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutcha, from Hindi, describes something rough or temporary, such as a building of dried mud.

clue.text: A row right away over the French watercolour

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: sending something away removes it, so the abbreviation for right is dropped once

parts.note: a row is a quarrel
standard abbreviation
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A row breaks out over a French watercolour, and someone storms away.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one of the two Rs in the row goes. In a down answer 'over' puts the first part on top of the French article.
explanation.definitionFit: An aquarelle is a painting in transparent watercolours, from the French word.

clue.text: Character well-informed on refined oil in tin

indicators.note: refining processes a crude substance into a new form, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: to be up on a subject is to be well informed about it

indicators.note: the mixed letters go inside the symbol for tin

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone well informed about refining oil and storing it in tins.
explanation.walkthrough: Sn, from Latin stannum, is the chemical symbol for tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Upsilon is a letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a written character.

clue.text: Timber producer okays different screening type

indicators.note: made different, the letters of okays are put in another order
a screen hides something behind or within it, so the outer letters surround the next word

parts.note: the five letters rearranged, split around the next piece
ilk means kind or type

explanation.surface: A timber merchant approves a different sort of screening.
explanation.definitionFit: The silky oak is an Australian tree grown for its decorative wood, so it produces timber.

clue.text: Illicit whiskey (term for it even in Chambers)

definitions.note: the answer is the plural noun

indicators.note: the pieces sit inside the word for chambers

parts.note: pos are chamber pots, plural of po

indicators.note: a term is an end point, so only the final letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: the end of the word
e'en is the poetic contraction of even

explanation.surface: A note that the term for illicit whiskey is listed even in the Chambers dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers looks like the dictionary every Mephisto solver uses, but it means chamber pots. A po is a chamber pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Poteen is Irish whiskey distilled privately without a licence, hence illicit.

clue.text: Take tea before noon and you fancy ceremony with it

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means to imagine freely, so the letters are freely rearranged

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
N is an abbreviation for noon
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An invitation to a tea party before midday that you might enjoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' in the definition points back to tea: the answer is a ceremony involving tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Chanoyu is the Japanese tea ceremony, a ritual preparation and serving of green tea.

clue.text: Bugle-call from large room on American Long Island

parts.note: a hall is a large room
standard abbreviation
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A bugle sounds from a big room on Long Island.
explanation.definitionFit: A hallali is a hunting horn call sounded when the quarry is brought to bay.

clue.text: Adult view in Pennsylvania shows a clumsy type

indicators.note: the earlier pieces are placed inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: standard US state abbreviation
A is the film certificate for adult
to view is to look

explanation.surface: An adult film viewed in Pennsylvania reveals someone awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: A is the old British film certificate for adult viewing.
explanation.definitionFit: Palooka is American slang for a stupid or clumsy person, originally a poor boxer.

clue.text: One vote's nothing for this looker

parts.note: a means one
a poll is a vote
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: In a beauty contest, one judge gives this good-looking person no votes at all.
explanation.definitionFit: An Apollo is a strikingly handsome young man, after the Greek god famed for his beauty.

clue.text: Shelter mentioned earlier taking cases

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it, so the cases go inside

parts.note: such refers back to something already mentioned
CA is an abbreviation for cases

explanation.surface: The shelter described earlier holds packing cases.
explanation.walkthrough: Such, as in 'such a thing', points back to something already mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: A succah is the temporary booth Jews build and live in during the festival of Sukkot.

clue.text: Join pieces of wood, say, dropping over for ditch outwork

indicators.note: dropping something lets it fall away, so that letter is lost

parts.note: to toenail is to fix two timbers with nails driven in at a slant
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A carpenter joins timbers to build a fortification beside a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: TOENAIL loses its O. 'Say' marks toenailing as one example of joining wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenail is a low fortification built in the ditch between two bastions.

clue.text: Dismal old blunt head in Lancing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an obsolete adjective for gloomy, from French
second meaning: the blunted tip of a jousting lance

explanation.surface: A gloomy old headmaster at Lancing, a school, speaks bluntly.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancing looks like the Sussex public school but means tilting with a lance.
explanation.definitionFit: Morne is both an old word for dreary and the rounded cap fixed on a tournament lance.

clue.text: Potter role put in play

indicators.note: putting something into play sets it moving, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as fodder
taken as written, as fodder

explanation.surface: A potter is given a part in a stage play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter' looks like a maker of pots but is the verb, to idle about.
explanation.definitionFit: To plouter is a Scots verb for dabbling or pottering aimlessly.

clue.text: Ma in concert edition was very unsettled

parts.note: Yo-Yo Ma is the famous cellist, in concert as a performer
ed. is the abbreviation for edition

explanation.surface: Mother was badly shaken by a particular edition of a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: Ma looks like mother but is the surname of the cellist Yo-Yo Ma.
explanation.definitionFit: To yo-yo is to swing repeatedly up and down, so something that yo-yoed fluctuated wildly.

clue.text: Kid tucking into last pieces of delicious sponge cake

indicators.note: tucking into food puts it inside, so one piece goes within the others
the last piece of each word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letters of the two words
to kid is to con or fool

explanation.surface: A child digs into the remains of a delicious sponge cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child but is the verb, to trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A scone is a small plain cake, often served with cream and jam.

clue.text: Units on a royal ship

parts.note: o' is a shortened form of on, as in o' nights
HMS, His or Her Majesty's Ship, prefixes Royal Navy vessel names

explanation.surface: Several military units are stationed aboard a navy vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: An ohm is the unit of electrical resistance.

clue.text: Growth in wine-making? Look in France and Florida

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the abbreviation for the country

parts.note: standard abbreviation
lo is an old exclamation meaning look
second meaning: .... is an abbreviation for Florida

explanation.surface: A question about vines growing in wine regions of France and Florida.
explanation.walkthrough: LO goes inside FR, and the answer is also an abbreviation of Florida.
explanation.definitionFit: Flor is the film of yeast that forms on sherry as it matures.

clue.text: On Metropolitan line, former chief's one up front

indicators.note: up front means placed ahead, so this piece comes before the line piece

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
arch as a prefix means chief, as in archbishop
a means one
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A former chief of London Underground puts one of his own in charge of the Metropolitan line.
explanation.walkthrough: Metropolitan line looks like the London Tube line; Metropolitan is the definition, a church title.
explanation.definitionFit: An exarch was a metropolitan bishop in the Eastern Church, so exarchal means relating to that rank.

clue.text: Flatter fairway, champion's flourished

indicators.note: read as 'has', the short form says one element has become another

parts.note: a fairway is the navigable channel of a river or harbour
ch. is an abbreviation for champion
fl., floruit, is the abbreviation for flourished

explanation.surface: Praise for a golf course: the fairway is excellent, and the champion has thrived on it.
explanation.walkthrough: In CHANNEL the CH becomes FL. Fairway looks like golf but is the sailing sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Flannel as a verb means to flatter or sweet-talk someone with evasive talk.

clue.text: Master bitten by dog — what language!

indicators.note: something bitten is held between the jaws, so it goes inside

parts.note: to dog someone is to tail them
M is an abbreviation for master

explanation.surface: An owner bitten by his dog lets out a stream of swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What language!' is the exclamation at bad words; the answer is an actual language.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamil is a Dravidian language of southern India and Sri Lanka.

clue.text: Journal agreed Hard Times novel for comic

parts.note: J is an abbreviation for journal

indicators.note: a novel version is a new one, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: OK means agreed
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
taken as written, as fodder

explanation.surface: A newspaper agrees that Dickens's novel Hard Times is good material for a comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: Hard Times looks like the Dickens title; only its H joins the anagram with TIMES.
explanation.definitionFit: A jokesmith is someone who crafts jokes, a comic writer or comedian.
